correctness.rationale: The distributional derivative yields an exact superposition of jumps and the Hilbert Bochner integral reduces the operator norm to these jumps. Exact integration on the unique cut dyadic cell yields 2^-j phi(2^j t); consecutive-scale pairing gives phi(u)+phi(2u)/2=1/3-3(d(u)-1/3)^2. Hence every even depth has exact nonnegative-square deficit and the only simultaneous zero sites are 1/3 and 2/3; geometric convergence justifies infinite depth. The first-level two-jump Gram determinant s(1-t)(t-s)>0 forces equality of general signed variations only for a point atom. Jensen yields the quantitative normalized variation location bound. Replayed exact-rational finite checker supports these analytical identities but is not the infinite proof.

The most relevant primary papers cover tent-based Takagi series, martingale restricted weak-type bounds, or Walsh matrix summability; individually optimized dyadic residual levels give only the weaker 1/2 bound. value.rationale: A cumulative multiresolution approximation error and its identical logarithmically weighted Haar energy are mathematically natural for BV data. The exact 4/9 sharp constant improves the componentwise 1/2 bound, yields an unexpected two-site one-third resonance at every even cutoff and infinite depth, and gives a structural variation-measure stability bound. This solves a complete natural scale family with substantive equality classification, not a routine reindexing or arbitrary finite computation.
